Free T4 normal. Cancer history with recent pembrolizumab — immune-related adverse events (irAE) must be considered prominently in differential.

patient.chief_complaint: Progressive weakness, shortness of breath, and inability to walk 7 days after second pembrolizumab cycle in patient with advanced uterine cancer.
patient.history_present_illness: Mrs. O. is a 70-year-old woman with stage IVB uterine adenocarcinoma currently receiving pembrolizumab and lenvatinib who presents 7 days after her second pembrolizumab cycle with progressive neurological deterioration. She was initially found to have a partial radiographic response on carboplatin-paclitaxel, but disease progressed and she was transitioned to pembrolizumab and lenvatinib. Seven days ago she received her second pembrolizumab infusion. Over the following days she developed new onset shortness of breath, painful swallowing, worsening fatigue, diffuse myalgias, and inability to walk. She developed a maculopapular rash on her trunk. She is unable to void spontaneously and required urinary catheterization. She has bilateral paresthesias in her hands and feet. On initial assessment, immunotherapy-related adverse events were the primary concern — pembrolizumab is known to cause immune-mediated myocarditis, hepatitis, pneumonitis, myositis, and neurological toxicity. The elevated TSH added concern for checkpoint inhibitor-mediated hypothyroidism, which was treated with levothyroxine. However, the progressive neurological weakness with hyporeflexia and the pattern of paresthesias is not fully explained by hypothyroidism or direct tumor invasion, raising the question of whether this represents GBS triggered by pembrolizumab immune dysregulation.

quantitative_data.pattern: Mixed axonal and demyelinating polyneuropathy with conduction block

specialized_test.impression: This is an ABNORMAL nerve conduction study. 1. Markedly prolonged distal motor latencies bilaterally (peroneal 8.2 ms, median 6.4 ms) with severely reduced conduction velocities (peroneal 28 m/s, median 38 m/s) and reduced CMAPs. 2. Absent sural SNAPs bilaterally. 3. Absent F-waves bilaterally in peroneal nerves; prolonged F-waves in median nerves. Absent H-reflex bilaterally. 4. No decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation at 3 Hz — NMJ transmission intact. Pattern consistent with mixed axonal and demyelinating polyneuropathy with conduction block. Clinical correlation recommended.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Guillain-Barré syndrome, immune checkpoint inhibitor-related (pembrolizumab-induced) — irAE

differential.key_features: Overlap of MG and GBS with ICIs (irAE syndromes); AChR antibodies, RNS, and single-fibre EMG; CK elevation and ocular involvement may co-occur.
CK elevation and myopathic EMG; reflexes are preserved; overlap syndromes with MG / GBS exist with ICIs.
Underlying advanced uterine cancer; CSF cytology, MRI brain / spine, and multifocal cranial neuropathies — different CSF profile (malignant cells, low glucose).
Subacute / chronic course typical; paraneoplastic panel testing covers.
Length-dependent sensory predominance, chronic course; absent areflexia; cannot account for acute weakness and CSF dissociation.

optimal_actions.action: Obtain CBC, CMP, HIV, anti-GM1/anti-GQ1b ganglioside antibodies, and stool culture / Campylobacter serology if recent diarrhea
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Mild leukocytosis / elevated inflammatory markers reflecting antecedent infection; ganglioside antibodies for variant typing; trigger identification (Campylobacter, CMV, EBV, Mycoplasma, HIV)

optimal_actions.action: Order nerve conduction studies and needle EMG (EMG/NCS)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Demyelinating pattern (prolonged DML, conduction block, reduced CV, absent F-waves) consistent with AIDP, or reduced CMAP amplitudes in axonal variants (AMAN/AMSAN)

optimal_actions.action: Perform lumbar puncture for CSF analysis
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Albuminocytologic dissociation — elevated protein with cell count <10/μL; may be normal in the first week of illness

optimal_actions.action: Order bedside respiratory function testing (FVC, MIP/MEP, NIF) and repeat every 4–6 hours
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Baseline and serial FVC, MIP/MEP, NIF; deterioration to FVC <20 mL/kg, MIP worse than -30 cmH2O, or VC <40% predicted triggers ICU transfer / intubation

optimal_actions.action: Search the medical literature for IVIG vs plasma exchange evidence to guide disease-modifying therapy
optimal_actions.expected_finding: IVIG (0.4 g/kg/day x 5 days) and plasma exchange are equivalently effective first-line therapies; combination not superior

optimal_actions.action: Check drug interactions / contraindications for IVIG (renal function, IgA deficiency screen) and/or plasma exchange (coagulation, calcium, hemodynamics)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Confirmation that IVIG can be given safely (no severe renal impairment, no IgA deficiency) or that plasma exchange is appropriate (adequate vascular access, stable coagulation)

optimal_actions.action: Obtain a 12-lead ECG to screen for autonomic dysrhythmias and baseline QTc
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Sinus tachycardia or bradycardia; conduction or repolarisation abnormalities reflecting autonomic involvement

optimal_actions.action: Initiate continuous cardiac telemetry for the first 1–2 weeks for moderate/severe disease — autonomic instability (bradyarrhythmias, BP lability) is common
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Documentation of sinus pauses, bradyarrhythmias, BP lability, or non-sustained tachyarrhythmias

useless_tools.rationale: GBS is a peripheral nerve / nerve-root disorder; EEG has no role in diagnosis unless atypical CNS features (encephalopathy, seizures) are present.
Echocardiography is not indicated in typical GBS; reserve for pre-existing cardiac disease or unexplained hemodynamic instability after autonomic causes are excluded.
Head CT contributes no diagnostic information in GBS; the disease is peripheral and CT does not visualise nerve roots reliably.
Functional / metabolic brain imaging adds no value in a peripheral demyelinating syndrome.
Cerebrovascular imaging is not indicated in a peripheral neuropathy without focal cerebral signs.
Brain MRI is reserved for atypical features (encephalopathy, CNS signs, transverse myelitis on differential). In classic GBS it does not aid diagnosis.

sequence_constraints.reason: Document respiratory status (FVC/NIF) before committing to IVIG vs plasma exchange — severe respiratory compromise mandates ICU triage and may influence treatment choice and timing.
Renal function, IgA screen, and CBC must be reviewed before IVIG to mitigate renal failure, anaphylaxis (IgA-deficient patients), and aseptic meningitis risk.

critical_actions: Hold pembrolizumab / lenvatinib pending oncology review.
Initiate high-dose IV corticosteroids (methylprednisolone 1–2 mg/kg/day) per ICI irAE management — ICI-related GBS is one of the few GBS contexts where steroids ARE indicated.
Add IVIG or plasma exchange for moderate-to-severe disease.
Coordinate with oncology / neurology multidisciplinary team.
Screen for overlap irAE syndromes (myositis, myocarditis) — CK, troponin, ECG.
contraindicated_actions: Do not resume pembrolizumab in confirmed grade 3–4 neurological irAE without specialist review.
Do not give IVIG without renal function review.
key_reasoning_points: ICI-related GBS is steroid-responsive — the standard 'no steroids in GBS' rule does not apply.
Overlap with irAE myositis and myocarditis (the 'triple-M' syndrome) carries high mortality and must be screened.
Distinguish from leptomeningeal carcinomatosis (CSF cytology, MRI brain/spine) and paraneoplastic neuropathy.

red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchor on paraneoplastic neuropathy or leptomeningeal carcinomatosis rather than ICI-related GBS.
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Temporal association with the second pembrolizumab cycle and classic GBS clinical pattern make irAE-GBS the leading diagnosis; oncologic causes remain on the differential but require positive evidence.

metadata.difficulty_description: Pembrolizumab-induced GBS in patient with active uterine cancer — competing diagnoses of paraneoplastic neuropathy, leptomeningeal carcinomatosis, and hypothyroidism irAE obscure the GBS diagnosis
metadata.difficulty_rationale: 6 required tools, 1 red herring(s); atypical or multi-comorbidity presentation requires substantial cross-modality synthesis and active rule-out of strong mimics.
case_body_concerns: Bedside respiratory function (FVC/MIP/MEP/NIF) is delivered via an `interpret_labs` followup panel rather than `order_specialized_test{test_type=respiratory_function}` as the criteria pack mandates. Agents calling order_specialized_test{respiratory_function} will hit the EMG/NCS output instead. Recommend adding a respiratory_function followup keyed to order_specialized_test in a follow-up case-body pass.
